sentences.text:
Seeking enhancement and also challenging the order of the Tribunal directing the insurance company to pay only 50% of the compensation on the ground that there was contributory negligence by the auto driver and the owner and insurer of the auto rickshaw are not made party, the petitioner has come up with this appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short).
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. FACTS:-

It is the case of the petitioner that on 15.02.2009 at about 5-30 p.m. he was returning to his village Mannalli along with his brother Sultan Salauddin in auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA.38/3838.

When they came near Yadlapur on Bidar-Mannalli road, a Maxi Cab bearing registration No.KA-38/2230 (hereinafter referred to as 'the offending vehicle'), driven by its driver in a rash or negligent manner, came from opposite side and dashed against the auto rickshaw.
3.1.
In the said accident, the petitioner and his brother sustained injuries.
Despite, prolonged treatment, they are not completely cured.
As owner and insurer, the respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
4. Respondent No.2 filed written statement disputing that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

It has also disputed the age, occupation, income of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by him and that they have resulted in permanent partial disability and also medical expenses incurred for the treatment.
The owner and insurer of auto rickshaw are necessary parties.
5. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.

6. Petitioner got himself examined as P.W.1 and relied upon Exs.P.1 to 22.
7.
On behalf of respondent No.2, R.W.1 is examined and Ex.R.1 is marked.

8. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by the petitioner granting compensation in a sum of Rs.43,800/- with interest at 6% per annum and Khaled Pasha @ Khaleel @Aju vs Sangappa S/O Basappa Madki And Anr on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164438239/
2 directed respondent No.2 to pay only 50% on the ground that there was contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the auto rickshaw.

sentences.text:
The details of the compensation granted are as below:
1. Pain and Suffering Rs.15,000/-
2. Medical Expenses Rs.1,800/-
3. Conveyance & Other Rs.2,000/- expenses 4. Loss of Income Rs.10,000/-

5 . Attendant and other Rs.5,000/- Sequential expenses 6. Inconvenience and Rs.10,000/-
discomfort Total Rs.43,800/-
9.
Respondent No.2 has not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
10. During the course of arguments, learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the compensation granted under all the heads is on the lower side.

The Tribunal has erred in holding that there was contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the auto rickshaw and as such,
respondent No.2 is liable to pay only 50% of the compensation.

He further submitted that similar order was passed in MVC No.251/2009 and the same is modified in MFA No.200578/2014 holding that as third parties, being the inmates of the auto rickshaw, the claimant and his brother have not contributed any negligence and it is a case of composite negligence and directed respondent No.2 insurance company to pay the entire compensation and the same has attained finality.

11. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 submitted that as held in MFA No.200578/2014, the entire liability may be fixed on respondent No.2 and globally marginal enhancement may be made.
12.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the records.

13. Based on the fact that there was more number of passengers than the permitted limit, the driver of the auto rickshaw was not holding a driving lience and after the accident, he ran away from the spot and it was plying on the wrong side of the road, the Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the driver of the auto rickshaw also contributed towards the accident.
Since the owner and insurer of auto rickshaw are not made party, the Tribunal has restricted the liability of respondent No.2 to 50%.
However, the said finding is reversed in MFA No.200578/2014, which is arising out of the same accident.

As held in the said judgment and award, as third parties, the inmates of the auto rickshaw including the petitioner are not responsible for causing the accident and as such, they cannot be denied 50% of the compensation.
It is a case of the composite negligence and not contributory negligence.

Therefore, the findings of the Tribunal that because of the driver of auto Khaled Pasha @ Khaleel @Aju vs Sangappa S/O Basappa Madki And Anr on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164438239/
3 rickshaw contributing 50% of the accident, the petitioner is not entitled for proportionate amount of the compensation, which is required to be set aside.
14.

sentences.text: Now coming to the quantum.
The accident is of the year 2009.
In the absence of proof of exact income, on notional basis, the income of the petitioner is held to be Rs.5,000/- p.m.

As per Ex.P.3,
the petitioner has suffered fracture of right clavicle and fracture of right 1st rib.
However, there is no evidence of any disability.

Having regard to the same, it would be reasonable to expect that the petitioner was under treatment for two months and therefore, grant of compensation in a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards loss of income, Rs.5,000/- for attendant and other sequential expenses is reasonable.

The Tribunal has granted the compensation of Rs.1,800/-
under the head medical expenses and Rs.2,000/- under the head conveyance and other expenses, which is on the lower side.
Having regard to the nature of the injuries suffered and the period of treatment, it would be appropriate to enhance the same by Rs.5,000/- each.

Since the petitioner has suffered fracture of right clavicle and right 1st rib, grant of Rs.15,000/- and Rs.10,000/- under the head pain and suffering &
inconvenience and discomfort is on the lower side.
The same are enhanced to Rs.20,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
15. Thus in all, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation in sum of Rs.60,000/- .

Pain and Suffering Rs.15,000/- Rs.20,000/-
2.

Medical Expenses Rs.1,800/- Rs.5,000/-
3. Conveyance & Rs.2,000/- Rs.5,000/-

Other expenses 4. Loss of Income Rs.10,000/- Rs.10,000/-
5. Attendant and Rs.5,000/- Rs.5,000/-
 other Sequential  expenses 6. Inconvenience and Rs.10,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 discomfort
Total Rs.43,800/-
16 . Of course the petitioner is entitled for the interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
As the insurer of the offending vehicle, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the entire compensation with accrued interest.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The Appeal is allowed in part.

4 (ii) The appellant is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.60,000/- as against Rs.43,800/-
granted by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a.
(iii) Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation amount together with interest within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.
(Minus the compensation already paid/deposited)
(iv) Send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.
